title: [30/9/2023] Daily oil production in 4 countries
prompt: The table below shows daily oil production in 4 countries from 2000 to 2004. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the daily oil production, measured in thousands of barrels, in four African countries over a five-year period from 2000 to 2004.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, Congo and Nigeria maintained their positions as the largest oil producers throughout the period. Chad and Somalia saw significant growth in their output while Congo experienced a steady decline in its production, and Nigeria's figures fluctuated during these years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the major oil-producing nations, Congo led the group with 275,000 barrels per day in 2000, which was 70,000 barrels higher than Nigeria's output. Congo's production subsequently decreased year by year, falling to 203,000 barrels daily by 2004. Meanwhile, Nigeria's figures showed some variation, dropping to 190,000 barrels in 2002 before recovering to reach 213,000 barrels per day in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining countries, both Chad and Somalia started with minimal production, at zero and 5,000 barrels per day respectively in 2000. Chad's output remained unchanged until 2003, when it began producing 8,000 barrels daily, before surging to 50,000 barrels in 2004. Similarly, Somalia's production rose consistently throughout the period, increasing more than tenfold from its initial figure to match Chad's output of 50,000 barrels per day by 2004.
